wizard.title: Calibration wizard
wizard.intro: We measure one stick at a time: rest, rotation, 8 directions and triggers. It takes about a minute. Nothing is written to the controller: the calibration lives in an app profile.

rest.title: Let go of the sticks
rest.body: Leave the controller still on a table and do not touch anything. We measure the centre for 2 seconds.

rotation.title: Rotate the {stick} stick along the edge
rotation.body: Push the stick against the edge and rotate slowly twice, then quickly twice. Do both directions if you can. No rush.
rotation.lowCoverage: Parts of the circle are still missing. Rotate a bit more or finish anyway.

directions.title: Push in 8 directions
directions.body: Push the {stick} stick all the way and hold for half a second in each direction. The arrow lights up once the direction is registered.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.releaseBody: Let go of both triggers. We measure where each one rests.
triggers.press: Press {trigger} all the way and hold
triggers.holdHint: Hold for about a second, then press Done.

wizard.demoNote: In demo mode the simulated controller makes every move by itself.
wizard.navPaused: During the wizard the controller does not navigate the app. Use mouse or keyboard.

report.title: {stick} stick report

issues.incompleteTravel: Does not reach full travel in some directions

circ.title: Circularity
circ.incomplete: The stick does not reach full travel in every direction. The suggested calibration already includes a rescale.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.incomplete: Does not reach 100 %: suggested max limit {pct}

suggestion.title: Suggested calibration
suggestion.body: Centre, deadzone and scale computed from the measurements. Your curve and sensitivity settings are kept.

report.hardwareNote: Software calibration does not fix mechanical wear. If the drift is large or grows over time, the stick module needs replacing.

adjust.title: Manual adjustments
adjust.antiDzHint: Cancels the game's own deadzone: the smallest movement already outputs this value.
adjust.curveHelp: Drag the points. Double-click an empty spot to add one; select a point and press Delete to remove it. Keyboard: Tab selects, arrows move (Shift moves further).
adjust.liveNote: The result applies to every screen: use Raw/Calibrated at the top to compare.

profiles.title: Profiles for {device}
profiles.confirmDelete: Delete profile "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
profiles.confirmReset: Reset "{name}" to factory default? Current settings will be lost.
profiles.hint: Each controller has its own profiles, identified by VID:PID and the serial number when available. Switch profiles with one click.

firmware.title: Calibration stored in the controller
firmware.intro: Writes the calibration into the controller itself, so it works everywhere: PS4/PS5, Switch, PC and every game. This is different from the software calibration in the other tabs, which only applies inside GamepadLab.
firmware.simulated: Simulated on the demo controller: nothing is written to a real controller.
firmware.notSupported: This controller does not accept firmware calibration.

whyNot.xbox: Xbox controllers have no public calibration command: the protocol is closed and the firmware is signed. Use the software calibration (Wizard and Adjust tabs).
whyNot.generic: Only DualShock 4, DualSense and Switch Pro have known firmware calibration. Use the software calibration (Wizard and Adjust tabs).

risks.title: Before you start
risks.wear: It does not fix drift caused by mechanical wear: in that case the stick module must be replaced.
risks.battery: Keep the battery above 30 % and the cable plugged in. If the controller dies in the middle of a permanent write, it may become unusable.
risks.noUndo: A permanent write on DualShock 4/DualSense cannot go back to the factory calibration: you can only write another one over it.
risks.tempFirst: That is why GamepadLab always calibrates in temporary mode first (gone when the controller turns off). You check the result and only then decide to make it permanent.
risks.credits: Sony commands ported from the open-source DualShock Calibration GUI project (MIT, the_al), the same one behind the PG Custom calibrator.

status.title: Controller state
status.unsaved: Temporary calibration active, not saved yet

blockers.bluetooth: Connect with a USB cable. Sony calibration cannot be done over Bluetooth.
blockers.clone: This looks like a clone or non-genuine controller: the factory commands do not work on it.
blockers.outdatedFirmware: The DualSense firmware is outdated (2020/2021). Update it from the console or Sony's official app and try again.
blockers.edgeNeedsHardwareMod: The DualSense Edge needs a hardware mod to store the module calibration. GamepadLab does not do that.
blockers.lowBattery: Battery below 30 %. Charge the controller before calibrating.
blockers.batteryUnknown: Could not read the battery. Move the controller for a few seconds or reconnect it.
blockers.pendingReboot: The controller is waiting for a reboot. Restart it and try again.

center.title: 1. Centre
center.quickBody: Let go of both sticks and do not touch the controller. The app takes 5 centre samples.
center.running: Calibrating the centre: do not close the app or unplug the controller.

corner.0: Move both sticks to the top-left corner and let go.
corner.1: Move both sticks to the top-right corner and let go.
corner.2: Move both sticks to the bottom-left corner and let go.
corner.3: Move both sticks to the bottom-right corner and let go.

center.whenCentered: When the sticks are back in the centre, press Continue.

range.title: 2. Range
range.body: Rotate both sticks slowly against the edge: at least 2 turns one way and 2 the other. Keep rotating even if the coverage climbs slowly.

check.title: 3. Check
check.body: Move the sticks and check: released, the dot should sit in the centre; rotating, it should touch the circle. For numbers, use the Wizard tab. Sony controllers ship with about 7 to 9 % average circularity error, and that is what games expect.

decide.title: 4. Decide
decide.body: The calibration is only active until the controller turns off. Choose what to do:
decide.ack: I understand a permanent save cannot go back to the factory calibration.
decide.confirmBody: The current calibration will be written to the controller's memory and work on any console or PC. Do not unplug the cable while it saves.
decide.discarded: Controller restarted: the temporary calibration was discarded.

switch.untested: Experimental: Switch Pro calibration writing has only been tested in simulation, not on a real controller yet.
switch.enableHint: The Switch Pro must be in full mode for the app to read and write its memory. If it stops responding in other apps, unplug and reconnect it.
switch.measureBody: For each stick: measure rest (released) and rotation (rotating against the edge).
switch.raised: Some ranges were below the minimum the console accepts and were raised: the stick may not reach 100 % on the console.
switch.writeConfirm: The user calibration (the same one the console writes in Calibrate Control Sticks) will be replaced. A backup of the current value is saved first. The factory calibration is never touched.
switch.written: Calibration written and verified. Backup at {path}
switch.clearConfirm: The controller will go back to its factory calibration. A backup is saved first.
switch.ack: I understand the risks of writing to the controller's memory.
